findings.title: Auth-only condition returned unparenthesized can leak rows when callers append AND clauses
findings.body: For org and team scope, `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns a top-level OR: `(teamId = ANY(..) AND isTeamBooking = true) OR (userId = ANY(..) AND isTeamBooking = false)`. In `getBaseConditions`, when a filter is also present, the auth part is wrapped in parentheses. When there is no filter, the auth condition is returned bare (line 75). Any caller that composes it as `WHERE ${base} AND "startTime" >= ...` gets the wrong precedence, because AND binds tighter than OR. The date, status or other filter then applies only to the last OR branch, so team bookings escape the extra filters. Because this value is the authorization boundary, `getBaseConditions` (or the reduce helpers) should always wrap the result in parentheses so it is safe to embed.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions: auth condition is never falsy
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy, falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`. So the `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `return NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. The code suggests auth is optional when it is not, and it hides the invariant that authorization is always applied. Simplify to `filterConditions ? sql\`(${auth}) AND (${filter})\` : auth`.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted although caching logic still exists
findings.body: The whole `Caching` describe block (auth and filter condition caching) was removed. `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and the `=== undefined` checks are still in the service, so the memoization behaviour is now untested. This includes the `null` filter case, where `null` is a valid cached value distinct from `undefined`. The tests should have been converted to the `Prisma.sql` form rather than dropped.

findings.title: New branching in team/org conditions has no test coverage
findings.body: The refactor adds conditional behaviour: the user-clause is omitted when `userIdsFromTeam` is empty (previously always emitted), and in org scope it is omitted when there are no member user IDs. The tests only cover the case where users exist. There is no test for a team scope whose team is not a child of the org (which should yield `NOTHING_CONDITION`), a team with no members, or an org with no child teams. These are the authorization edge cases the PR checklist itself calls out.
